tagline: From Sonoran Desert to ponderosa pine, through one tunnel.
intro: US 60 sets out east from near Florence Junction across the Sonoran Desert, past Picketpost Mountain, named by soldiers camped at its foot in 1870, who used it as a lookout. An oddly placed mailbox on the summit holds the trail log. The road runs through Superior, an old silver and then copper town under Apache Leap, and climbs on toward Miami.
In 35 miles it passes through four biotic communities, from the Sonoran Desert up to ponderosa pine, with riparian stretches along Arnett and Pinto creeks.

moments.title: Boyce Thompson Arboretum
moments.text: A mining engineer's desert garden along Queen Creek since 1924, with more than 2,600 arid-land species and one of the country's largest red gum eucalyptus, known as Mr. Big.

moments.title: Queen Creek Tunnel
moments.text: Just east of Superior the road climbs at a six percent grade through 1,217 feet of solid rock. At the 1952 dedication a brass band stood on the drill rig.

moments.title: Top-of-the-World
moments.text: The divide between Superior and Miami, at about 4,600 feet, properly called Mason's Valley. The name came from a 1922 campground two miles west and stuck here anyway, an unfortunate misnomer by one account.

sources.label: USDA Forest Service, Tonto National Forest, Gila-Pinal Scenic Road
